title: Conveyor vs Arphie (2026): A Buyer's Comparison for Security-Questionnaire and RFP Teams
summary: Conveyor vs Arphie compared on AI accuracy, pricing, integrations and G2 reviews, and where an AI-agentic alternative fits for security-questionnaire teams.
body_markdown:
Both Conveyor and Arphie are recent, AI-native entrants aimed at cutting the hours teams spend on[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/security-questionnaire) , DDQs and RFPs. They take different routes to the same problem. This guide compares them on architecture, features, pricing, integrations and verified reviews so you can decide which fits your workflow — not which one a vendor wants you to buy.


**Last reviewed:** January 2026. This comparison draws on each vendor's published materials, verified G2 and Capterra reviews, and independent third-party write-ups (SiftHub, Responsive, Software Advice). Both products price on a quote or usage basis and ship changes often, so read every figure below as a point-in-time snapshot. Confirm current pricing, plan caps and integration coverage with each vendor before you sign anything.


## **TL;DR: Conveyor vs Arphie in Three Sentences**


Conveyor fits teams whose center of gravity is security review — a public Trust Center for customer self-service plus an AI agent that answers inbound security questionnaires with cited sources. Arphie fits teams that want AI agents drafting RFP, DDQ and security-questionnaire answers from knowledge that already lives in Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Seismic or Highspot, without maintaining a separate library.


Which is better depends on what your team needs — lead with Conveyor if trust-portal self-service is the priority, lead with Arphie if broad RFP/DDQ coverage across connected sources matters more; buyers comparing the two are also increasingly benchmarking a newer class of AI-agentic response platforms as a third reference point.

## What Should You Consider When Choosing Between Conveyor and Arphie?


Short answer: match the tool to your dominant use case (security review vs. broad RFP/DDQ), then pressure-test AI accuracy, source coverage and pricing during a demo. Use these criteria as your checklist:


**• Primary use case:** Is your volume mostly inbound security questionnaires, or a mix of RFPs, DDQs and security reviews?


**• AI drafting quality:** How accurate are first drafts on your real content, and how much editing do they need?


**• Hallucination control:** Does each answer ship with a citation and[a confidence signal you can verify](https://www.inventive.ai/rfp-software-faq/ai-rfp-tools-prevent-hallucinations) ?


**• Knowledge management:** Do you want a managed library, or AI that pulls from where content already lives?


**• Customer self-service:** Do you need a public trust portal so prospects answer their own security questions?


**• Content governance:** How does the tool flag stale or conflicting answers before they ship?


**• Integrations:** Does it connect to your CRM, ticketing, docs and content stores? (See the integrations table below.)


**• Workflow and collaboration:** Can you assign questions, track ownership and route approvals?


**• Export and format flexibility:** Can it handle[Excel questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/rfp-software-faq/how-ai-handles-excel-questionnaires) and narrative proposals both?


**• Security and compliance:** What certifications and data-handling policies apply?


**• Analytics and reporting:** Can you see cycle times, throughput and content gaps?


**• Pricing and total cost:** Per-seat vs. per-project vs. usage-based — model your real volume. The[RFP software comparison guide](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-software-comparison-guide) walks through how to compare quote-based vendors on a like-for-like basis.


**• Ease of implementation:** How long until the first useful draft, and how heavy is admin setup?


**• Maturity and reviews:** How deep is the verified review base for the size of your rollout?

## AI Capabilities: How Each Tool Drafts Answers


Both platforms are built AI-first and both attach source citations and confidence signals to answers so reviewers can validate quickly rather than trust blindly.


### **Conveyor**


**•** AI agent focuses on security questionnaires, drawing on CRM and ticketing intake.


**•** Answers are cited back to source documents with confidence scoring, which reviewers say reduces manual review.


**•** Reviewers describe strong automation on "the more standard questions."


### **Arphie**


**•** AI agents draft across RFPs, DDQs and security questionnaires from a managed knowledge base.


**•** Live connections pull from Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Seismic and Highspot, so drafts reflect current content.


**•** Each answer shows exact source citations and confidence signals; reviewers report it is "fast and accurate."


**Note (applies to both):** Neither product's review base is as deep as legacy RFP platforms, and AI draft quality varies with the quality of your underlying content. Test both on your own edge-case questions before deciding. If cross-document consistency and automatic conflict detection are priorities, benchmark them against an AI-agentic approach in the[best AI agent for security questionnaires roundup](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-ai-agent-for-security-questionnaires) .

The architectures pull integrations in opposite directions. Conveyor's connectors — Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira and Claude — mostly feed its agent from CRM and ticketing systems, which suits a security-review team routing inbound questionnaire requests. Arphie's connectors lean toward content stores (Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Seismic, Highspot) plus website ingestion, so drafts pull from where source knowledge already sits.


Two caveats to verify in a demo: Arphie reviewers report its Salesforce integration is less mature than some rivals, and Conveyor reviewers flag gaps around the browser extension and API. Confirm the exact connectors, direction of sync, and whether each is one-way or bidirectional before you commit, connector names on a marketing page rarely tell you how deep the integration actually goes.


## Conveyor: Overview, Features and Reviews


Conveyor pairs an AI agent for security questionnaires with a customer-facing Trust Center, so prospects can self-serve security documents while your team automates repetitive questionnaire responses. It has been in market longer than Arphie, reflected in a larger G2 review base.


### **Best features**


**•** AI agent automates standard security-questionnaire responses.


**•** Answers cited back to source documents with confidence scoring, reducing manual review.


**•** Trust Center centralizes security document sharing and enables customer self-service.


**•** Reviewers report an intuitive, easy-to-use interface that speeds response cycles.


**•** Time-saving on RFP and questionnaire completion is a recurring theme in reviews.


**•** CRM and ticketing intake (Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira) feeds the agent.


### **Limitations (**[sourced as per G2](https://www.g2.com/products/conveyor-conveyor/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) **)**


**•** Reviewers note missing features, particularly around the browser extension and API capabilities.


**•** Occasional slow loading times reported during urgent tasks.


**•** Initial setup and configuration can be intricate for admins; onboarding support was flagged in a review.


**•** Security-questionnaire automation is gated to the paid Professional plan, per the vendor's own blog.


**•** Public pricing is inconsistent across sources (see below), making budgeting harder without a quote.


**•** Buyers weighing the Trust Center against broader RFP coverage sometimes shortlist other options, the[Conveyor alternatives and competitors overview](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/conveyor-alternatives-competitors) lays out where each fits.


### **Ratings and reviews**


**•** G2: **4.6 / 5** across 150 reviews ([G2](https://www.g2.com/products/conveyor-conveyor/reviews) ).


**•** Capterra:[listing exists](https://www.capterra.com/p/235709/Conveyor/) , but no verifiable rating/count was found.


**•** TrustRadius: no verified rating located.


**Positive:** "It's super easy to use and the AI functionality is great to automate the more standard questions." — G2 review


**Mixed:** "The initial configuration, especially for admins, can be intricate." — G2 revi[ew](https://www.g2.com/products/conveyor-conveyor/pricing)


**Comparing security-questionnaire automation approaches?** One team reports 90% faster RFPs with zero weekend hours lost after moving to an agentic platform —[see the 90%-faster case study](https://www.inventive.ai/case-studies/best-rfp-software--90-faster-rfps-0-weekend-hours-lost) .


## **Arphie: Overview, Features and Reviews**


Arphie is an AI-native platform for RFPs, DDQs and security questionnaires, built around AI agents that draft from a managed, live-connected knowledge base. Rather than maintaining a separate content library, it connects to where content already lives Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Seismic, Highspot. and drafts from there.


### **Best features**


**•** AI agents draft answers across RFPs, DDQs and security questionnaires.


**•** Live connections to Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Seismic and Highspot pull from existing content.


**•** Each answer shows exact source citations and confidence signals for fast validation.


**•** Reviewers describe it as highly intuitive with fast setup and onboarding.


**•** Strong reported time-savings on RFP responses.


**•** Website/URL ingestion adds public content as a source.


### **Limitations (**[as per G2](https://www.g2.com/products/arphie/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) **)**


**•** Lack of mobile accessibility is the most consistently cited limitation


**•** Limited export options (only Excel imports for Q&A pairs), with file import/export and reporting features pending (


**•** Salesforce integration reported as less mature than some competitors


**•** Reporting functionality reported as inadequate or pending


**•** Newer market position with a thin, recent review base


**•** Teams that want deeper reporting or mobile access often widen the shortlist — the[Arphie alternatives and competitors overview](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/arphie-alternative-competitors) compares the main options.


### **Ratings and reviews**


**•** G2: **4.9 / 5** across 19 reviews (G2) — note the alternatives page reports 19 while the reviews listing shows ~16; the sample is small either way.


**•** Capterra: **5.0 / 5** based on 1 review ([Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/10017918/Arphie/) ) — very thin.


**•** TrustRadius: no verified rating located. Arphie also has a[Gartner Peer Insights profile](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/product/arphie) , but no verified star rating/count could be isolated.


**Positive:** "It's fast and accurate, allowing me to save time by focusing only on the difficult questions that matter." — G2 review


**Mixed:** "Arphie was great to use but is not something I would use long term in my particular work setting." —[Software Advice review](https://www.softwareadvice.com/rfp/arphie-profile/)

## **How Much Does Conveyor Cost?**


Conveyor has a free Trust Center tier and a quote/usage-based paid plan. The **free** tier caps at roughly 120 companies/year with limited documents, Q&As and Conveyor branding. Paid **Professional** pricing is quote/usage-based, priced on trust-center download volume and/or the number of questionnaires and RFPs processed by AI, with volume discounts.


Reported starting prices disagree: G2 lists a starting price of **$9,600/yr** (G2 pricing), while Conveyor's own comparison blog cites a Professional plan starting at **$4,800** (Conveyor blog), reported (confirm on the live listing). Note that security-questionnaire automation sits on the paid Professional plan, not the free tier. For a fuller feature-and-pricing breakdown, see the[Conveyor AI pricing and features review](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/conveyor-ai-pricing-features-reviews) .


## **How Much Does Arphie Cost?**


Arphie does not publish pricing. It uses **custom, quote-based** pricing built on team size, annual RFP/questionnaire volume and integration needs, with a flat per-project model and unlimited users rather than per-seat fees; there is no standard free trial (trial on request).


This is reported (confirm with vendor) via SiftHub and corroborated by Responsive's comparison glossary; the[Arphie pricing, features and review breakdown](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/arphie-pricing-features-reviews) covers what to ask for in a quote. The unlimited-user model can favor larger teams, but without published tiers you'll need a written quote to compare it against Conveyor's usage-based figures.


**Note (applies to both):** Quote-based pricing means the sticker figures floating online may not reflect your deal. Ask each vendor for a written quote tied to your seat count, volume and integrations, and compare on total cost — not headline numbers.


Building your budget case? AssetWorks reports a 422% ROI and roughly $105K in net savings from RFP automation.[See how AssetWorks measured the return](https://www.inventive.ai/case-studies/how-assetworks-facilities-achieved-422-roi-on-rfp-automation-with-inventive-ai) .


## **Is Conveyor Better Than Arphie?**


Neither is universally better, it depends on your dominant workflow. Conveyor is the stronger fit when customer-facing security self-service (the Trust Center) is central and you want a longer-tenured product with a deeper review base. Arphie is the stronger fit when you need AI agents drafting across RFPs, DDQs and security questionnaires from content that already lives in your document and enablement systems, and you value fast onboarding.


Weigh the trade-offs honestly: Conveyor reviewers flag intricate admin setup and browser-extension/API gaps; Arphie reviewers flag missing mobile access, limited exports and pending reporting. Both have thinner review histories than legacy platforms. Run a side-by-side pilot on your real questionnaires before deciding. For a structured scoring approach across categories, the[enterprise RFP software comparison](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-top-enterprise-rfp-software-comparison) is a useful framework.


## **Security, Content Governance and Reviews**


Both tools cite answers to sources and attach confidence signals, the baseline for hallucination control. Where they differ: Conveyor's Trust Center adds a governed, customer-facing document layer, so prospects pull approved security artifacts directly, while Arphie's live connections keep drafts tied to whatever the current source content says.


Neither approach removes the governance work of keeping that underlying content accurate — Conveyor still relies on the documents you publish to the portal, and Arphie's drafts are only as current as the connected repositories. Ask each vendor how stale or conflicting answers get surfaced, who owns approving them, and whether the system flags contradictions across a full response or only answer-by-answer. Confirm each vendor's certifications (e.g., SOC 2) and data-handling policies directly, since these change and were not fully verifiable in public sources at time of writing.


On reviews, remember the asymmetry: Conveyor's 4.6/5 sits on 150 G2 reviews; Arphie's 4.9/5 sits on ~19, and its Capterra 5.0 rests on a single review. A higher average on a small, recent sample carries less weight than a slightly lower average on a larger one. Read the individual reviews, not just the star average — and check whether reviewers match your company size and use case.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Is Conveyor better than Arphie?**


Neither wins outright. Conveyor is better for teams centered on security review with a customer-facing Trust Center and a deeper review base (4.6/5, 150 G2 reviews). Arphie is better for teams drafting RFPs, DDQs and security questionnaires from live-connected content sources, with fast onboarding (4.9/5 on a smaller 19-review sample). Match the tool to your dominant use case and pilot both.


### **How much does Conveyor cost?**


Conveyor offers a free Trust Center tier (capped at ~120 companies/year with limits and branding). Its paid Professional plan is quote/usage-based; reported starting prices range from $4,800 (Conveyor's blog) to $9,600/yr (G2). Because pricing is usage-based, request a written quote for your volume, reported figures should be confirmed on the live listing.


### **How much does Arphie cost?**


Arphie does not publish pricing. It uses custom, quote-based pricing built on team size, annual volume and integrations, with a flat per-project model and unlimited users rather than per-seat fees. There's no standard free trial (trial on request). Confirm current terms directly with Arphie.


### **Do Conveyor and Arphie both handle RFPs, or just security questionnaires?**


Both handle more than security questionnaires, but with different emphasis. Conveyor centers on security review — an AI agent for security questionnaires plus a customer-facing Trust Center — while also processing RFPs on its Professional plan. Arphie is built for a broader mix of RFPs,[DDQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-due-diligence-questionnaires) and security questionnaires from the start, drafting from live-connected content sources. If RFP breadth is your priority, weigh Arphie's model; if inbound security self-service dominates your workload, weigh Conveyor's Trust Center.


### **What do reviewers say are the biggest limitations of each tool?**


For Conveyor, G2 reviewers cite missing browser-extension and API features, occasional slow loading during urgent tasks, and intricate admin setup. For Arphie, reviewers most often cite the lack of mobile access, limited export options, and reporting that is inadequate or still pending, alongside a thin, recent review base per SiftHub. Test these specific areas against your workflow during a trial rather than relying on the headline star rating.


### **What is an alternative to Conveyor and Arphie?**


Beyond these two, buyers commonly evaluate legacy RFP platforms (Loopio, Responsive, Qvidian) and a newer class of AI-agentic response platforms. Inventive AI is one example of the AI-agentic category: rather than a trust portal or a managed content library, agents run intake, drafting, governance and validation, with humans approving the output. RAD AI reports[2× more accurate responses than other RFP AI tools it tested](https://www.inventive.ai/case-studies/inventive-ai-2x-more-accurate-responses-than-other-rfp-ai-tools-barely-needing-a-tweak) . For a wider view of the field, the[best RFP software roundup](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-rfp-software) compares the main options side by side.
